origin.description: Count words in each string, ignoring non-word boundary segments.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

origin.details: Equivalent to stri_count_boundaries(str, type = "word", skip_word_none = TRUE, locale = locale). Spaces and punctuation are UBRK_WORD_NONE and are not counted. A missing string is NA. An empty string counts as 0. A locale whose break data falls back to root warns.
origin.value: An integer vector the same length as str.
origin.example:
x <- stri_count_words("one two three")
cat(paste0('stri_count_words("one two three") returns ', x, '.\n'))

translation.description: Count words in each string, ignoring non-word boundary segments.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

translation.details: Calls stri_count_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none true. Non-word segments are not counted. NA stays missing. The string "NA" is text. An empty string counts as 0. Thai word data falls back to root and warns. Japanese word data does not.
translation.value: A list of ints. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_count_words
x = stri_count_words("one two three")
print(f'stri_count_words("one two three") returns {x[0]}.')
